title: Chemists isolate stable oxoboranes after 60 years

sources.cita_corta: Lubczyk et al. (2026). Synthesis and isolation of stable oxoboranes. Nature Chemistry.
supports: Three room-temperature-stable oxoboranes isolated as crystalline solids
B–O bonds 1.208(4)–1.217(4) Å, exceptionally short and strong
Simple synthesis from diboracumulene and carbonyls at room temperature
Previously sought for over 60 years, thought too unstable

sources.cita_corta: University of Würzburg news (2026). A 60-Year search is over.
supports: Holger Braunschweig team at Uni Würzburg
Nearly everybody had given up on isolating oxoboranes
Supported by computational work from Tezpur University

scenes.narration: For more than sixty years, chemists thought it impossible to isolate oxo-boranes: molecules with a triple bond between boron and oxygen, too unstable for the lab.
scenes.visual_description: pop art comic of frustrated chemists in lab with exploding molecule diagrams and bold POW effects

scenes.narration: At the University of Würzburg, Holger Braunschweig's team, with computational support from Tezpur, reacted a reactive diboracumulene with simple ketones at room temperature.
scenes.visual_description: pop art comic university building in Würzburg with comic speech bubbles of chemical reaction
scenes.image_prompt: pop art comic book panel, Ben-Day halftone dots, bold black outlines, saturated primary colors, dramatic action burst background, vertical 9:16, no text + pop art comic university building in Würzburg with comic speech bubbles of chemical reaction

scenes.narration: The surprise was total: they formed three stable oxo-boranes as orange and yellow crystalline solids, with over fifty percent isolated yield.
scenes.visual_description: pop art comic of glowing orange and yellow crystal solids popping out of a reaction flask
scenes.image_prompt: pop art comic book panel, Ben-Day halftone dots, bold black outlines, saturated primary colors, dramatic action burst background, vertical 9:16, no text + pop art comic of glowing orange and yellow crystal solids popping out of a reaction flask

scenes.narration: The boron-oxygen bonds measure between 1.208 and 1.217 angstroms. They are extremely short and strong, almost perfectly linear, with evidence of a real triple bond.
scenes.visual_description: pop art comic close-up of B≡O triple bond with measurement lines and atomic models
scenes.image_prompt: pop art comic book panel, Ben-Day halftone dots, bold black outlines, saturated primary colors, dramatic action burst background, vertical 9:16, no text + pop art comic close-up of B triple bond O with measurement lines and atomic models

scenes.narration: Before, these species had only been detected in the gas phase or in cryogenic matrices. Never as stable compounds at room temperature.
scenes.visual_description: pop art comic split panel of cold matrix isolation vs room temperature crystals
scenes.image_prompt: pop art comic book panel, Ben-Day halftone dots, bold black outlines, saturated primary colors, dramatic action burst background, vertical 9:16, no text + pop art comic split panel of cold matrix isolation versus room temperature crystals

scenes.narration: The finding opens paths to prepare more elusive molecules of the p-block. Almost everyone in the field had given up the search decades ago.
scenes.visual_description: pop art comic of abandoned lab notebooks transforming into new molecular structures
scenes.image_prompt: pop art comic book panel, Ben-Day halftone dots, bold black outlines, saturated primary colors, dramatic action burst background, vertical 9:16, no text + pop art comic of abandoned lab notebooks transforming into new molecular structures

scenes.narration: Now chemists can study them, manipulate them, and build new structures. A sixty-year paradigm of failed attempts broke in an unexpected way.
